practiceQuestions.q: Who was the founder of the Sindhia dynasty of Gwalior?
practiceQuestions.sol: Ranoji Sindhia was the founder of the Sindhia dynasty. He started as a personal attendant (bargir) of Peshwa Baji Rao I and rose to prominence, eventually securing a jagir in Malwa. [Primary Reference: NCERT History / Standard Maratha History Texts]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the original traditional capital of the Sindhia territories before Gwalior became their primary seat?
practiceQuestions.sol: Ujjain was the original capital of the Sindhia family in Malwa before Mahadji Sindhia shifted the administrative and political hub to Gwalior. [Primary Reference: NCERT History / Gazetteer of Gwalior State]

practiceQuestions.q: Which famous French military commander was employed by Mahadji Sindhia to modernize his infantry and artillery?
practiceQuestions.sol: Count Benoît de Boigne was hired by Mahadji Sindhia to organize, train, and command his European-style disciplined brigades, which became the most formidable native army in 18th-century India. [Primary Reference: Modern Indian History by Bipan Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: In which landmark battle of 1761 did the Sindhias participate alongside other Maratha forces against Ahmad Shah Abdali?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Sindhias fought in the Third Battle of Panipat (1761) under Sadashivrao Bhau, suffering heavy casualties, including the death of Jankoji Rao Sindhia. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 History]

practiceQuestions.q: Who conferred upon Mahadji Sindhia the title of 'Wakil-ul-Mutlaq' (Regent of the Empire) on behalf of the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II?
practiceQuestions.sol: Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II conferred the supreme title of Wakil-ul-Mutlaq on Mahadji Sindhia in 1785, making him the effective vice-regent of the Mughal Empire. [Primary Reference: Spectrum's A Brief History of Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q: The Treaty of Surji-Anjangaon (1803) was signed between the British and which Sindhia ruler?
practiceQuestions.sol: Following defeats in the Second Anglo-Maratha War, Daulat Rao Sindhia signed the Treaty of Surji-Anjangaon in 1803, ceding extensive territories to the British East India Company. [Primary Reference: Modern Indian History by Bipan Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: Which caste did the Sindhia dynasty belong to?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Sindhias belonged to the Kunbi (Maratha) caste, similar to other major Maratha houses like the Bhonsles and Gaekwads. [Primary Reference: NCERT History / Socio-Political Structure of Maratha Empire]

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the ruler of Gwalior during the Indian Revolt of 1857?
practiceQuestions.sol: Jayajirao Sindhia was the ruler of Gwalior during the Revolt of 1857. Though his troops rebelled and joined the forces of Tantia Tope and Rani Lakshmibai, Jayajirao himself remained loyal to the British. [Primary Reference: Spectrum's A Brief History of Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which famous palace was built by the Sindhia rulers in Gwalior, reflecting European architecture combined with Indian motifs?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Jai Vilas Palace was built by Jayajirao Sindhia in 1874, designed by Sir Michael Filose, showcasing a blend of Tuscan, Italian, and Corinthian architectural styles. [Primary Reference: Archaeological Survey of India / MP Tourism]

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the last ruling Maharaja of Gwalior state who signed the Instrument of Accession to independent India in 1947?
practiceQuestions.sol: Maharaja Jiwajirao Scindia was the last reigning monarch of Gwalior state, who acceded to the Dominion of India and later served as the Rajpramukh of Madhya Bharat. [Primary Reference: White Paper on Indian States, Ministry of States]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Mahadji Sindhia's military reorganization fundamentally alter the nature of Maratha warfare in the late 18th century?
opts: He completely abolished cavalry in favor of infantry and guerrilla tactics.
He integrated European-style disciplined infantry and modern artillery under European officers, moving away from traditional light guerrilla cavalry.
He relied solely on British mercenary troops without training native soldiers.
He rejected firearms and focused exclusively on hand-to-hand combat weapons.
practiceQuestions.sol: Traditionally, Marathas relied on rapid guerrilla cavalry (bargirs). Mahadji Sindhia recognized the superiority of European infantry and artillery formations, employing officers like de Boigne to raise standing regular brigades, thereby transforming his military into a modern professional force. [Primary Reference: Modern Indian History by Bipan Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the strategic significance of the Sindhias securing the custody of the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II?
opts: It allowed them to legitimize their political and territorial ambitions under the imperial umbrella.
It gave them direct control over Bengal's revenues through Mughal taxation laws.
It forced the British to surrender Calcutta to the Maratha Confederacy.
It enabled them to abolish the caste system across northern India.
practiceQuestions.sol: By acting as protectors of the Mughal Emperor, the Sindhias wielded enormous moral and political leverage. Issuing imperial decrees in the Emperor's name legitimized Maratha hegemony over North India and gave their administrative actions constitutional backing. [Primary Reference: NCERT History / Spectrum History]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the relationship between the Sindhias and the Peshwas evolve during the latter half of the 18th century?
opts: The Sindhias remained subservient tax-collectors with no independent foreign policy.
The Sindhias grew into virtually autonomous power brokers who often dominated Pune politics while nominally respecting the Peshwa.
The Sindhias completely broke away from the Maratha Confederacy and allied with the Mughals against Pune.
The Peshwas directly administered Gwalior through appointed Chitpavan governors.
practiceQuestions.sol: While nominally acknowledging the Peshwa's supremacy, Mahadji Sindhia amassed such vast military and financial resources in northern India that he became the most powerful figure in the Maratha Confederacy, often arbitrating succession disputes in Pune. [Primary Reference: Modern Indian History by Bipan Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the consequence of the Second Anglo-Maratha War on the territorial integrity and sovereignty of the Sindhia state?
opts: They gained full control over Delhi and Agra from the British.
They lost valuable territories including Agra, Delhi, Broach, and parts of Gujarat, and had to accept a British Resident.
The Sindhia state was completely annexed and dissolved into British India.
They formed a permanent military alliance with the French to oust the British.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Treaty of Surji-Anjangaon (1803) stripped Daulat Rao Sindhia of his territories between the Ganga and Yamuna, Ahmadnagar, Broach, and parts of Gujarat, reducing Gwalior to a subsidiary ally of the British. [Primary Reference: Spectrum's A Brief History of Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the economic base of the Sindhia state differ from that of smaller Maratha principalities during their peak?
opts: They depended solely on maritime trade in the Indian Ocean.
They combined rich agricultural revenue from Malwa with systematic tribute collection (chauth/sardeshmukhi) and revenue administration across northern territories.
They relied entirely on loans from European banking institutions.
They prohibited agrarian production to focus exclusively on munitions manufacturing.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Sindhias built a robust fiscal-military state. By controlling the fertile Malwa plateau, collecting northern tributes, and establishing efficient revenue collection systems, they sustained large regular standing armies and artillery parks. [Primary Reference: Economic History of India / Maratha Administrative Systems]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of the Battle of Lalsot (1787) for Mahadji Sindhia?
opts: It was an unmitigated victory that expanded Maratha control into the Punjab.
It was a setback against Rajput confederacies (Jaipur and Jodhpur) that tested his political resilience and exposed limitations in facing allied Rajput forces.
It marked the final annexation of Awadh by the Sindhia forces.
It resulted in a permanent military treaty between the Sindhias and the British East India Company.
practiceQuestions.sol: At the Battle of Lalsot, Mahadji Sindhia faced a combined coalition of Rajput rulers (Jaipur and Jodhpur). Though indecisive/a check for Mahadji, it temporarily halted Maratha expansion in Rajasthan, though he quickly recovered through diplomatic maneuvering. [Primary Reference: Jadunath Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the Sindhia dynasty's stance toward the 1857 Revolt shape its subsequent relationship with the British Crown?
opts: Active participation against the British led to the confiscation of all Gwalior territories.
The ruler's loyalty to the British, despite military mutiny within his ranks, earned him British trust, substantial honors, and retention of autonomous princely status.
The ruler abdicated in favor of Rani Lakshmibai to establish a joint Maratha-Mughal state.
The state was transformed into a directly administered British province.
practiceQuestions.sol: Maharaja Jayajirao Sindhia remained steadfastly loyal to the British during the 1857 revolt, even when his own army revolted. The British rewarded this loyalty by restoring his territories, conferring honors, and considering Gwalior a key pillar of stability in Central India. [Primary Reference: Imperial Gazetteer of India / Cambridge History of India]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the administrative and political structure of the Maratha Confederacy, and where did the Sindhias fit into this framework?
opts: A centralized unitary state where the Peshwa directly appointed all provincial governors.
A confederation of semi-autonomous chiefdoms (Sindhia, Holkar, Gaekwad, Bhonsle) acknowledging the Peshwa as nominal head while operating independently in their respective spheres.
A feudal monarchy controlled entirely by the Sindhia family over all other Maratha clans.
A democratic republic with elected representatives from each Maratha province.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Maratha Confederacy operated as a loose union of prominent chiefs. The Sindhias dominated northern and central India (Gwalior/Malwa), operating with high autonomy while coordinating with Pune on pan-Maratha matters. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 History / Bipan Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Mahadji Sindhia's interactions with the Rajput states shape political stability in Western and Northern India?
opts: He established harmonious matrimonial alliances that permanently pacified all Rajput kingdoms without conflict.
His attempts to extract heavy tributes and assert Maratha hegemony generated friction, leading to complex military and diplomatic tussles with Rajput polities.
He completely absorbed Rajasthan into the Gwalior state administration, dissolving Rajput principalities.
He relinquished all claims over Rajasthan in exchange for British protection.
practiceQuestions.sol: Mahadji's push to collect tribute and assert dominance over Rajput states like Jaipur, Jodhpur, and Udaipur created continuous friction. While it brought temporary financial gains, it also united Rajput resistance, exemplified at the Battle of Lalsot. [Primary Reference: Jadunath Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the ultimate fate of the Gwalior princely state post-India's independence in 1947?
opts: It remained an independent sovereign nation outside the Indian Union.
It merged into the Union of India, becoming part of the newly formed 'Madhya Bharat' state, with the Maharaja serving as Rajpramukh.
It was partitioned between Pakistan and India due to religious demographics.
It was converted into a Union Territory directly administered by the President of India.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's integration policy, Maharaja Jiwajirao Scindia signed the covenant to merge Gwalior into the United State of Gwalior, Indore, and Malwa (later Madhya Bharat), accepting the position of Rajpramukh (Governor). [Primary Reference: White Paper on Indian States, Ministry of States]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Ranoji Sindhia:
1. He was the founder of the Sindhia dynasty and began his career as a personal servant (bargir) of Peshwa Baji Rao I.
2. He established his primary administrative capital at Gwalior right at the inception of his rule in the early 18th century.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Ranoji Sindhia founded the dynasty and rose from being a bargir (trooper/attendant) under Baji Rao I. Statement 2 is incorrect: Ranoji's primary seat was Ujjain in Malwa; it was Mahadji Sindhia who later shifted the political hub and capital to Gwalior. [Primary Reference: NCERT History / Maratha Genealogies]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Mahadji Sindhia:
1. He played a crucial role in reviving Maratha power in northern India after the disaster of the Third Battle of Panipat (1761).
2. He modernized his army with the help of the French military adventurer Benoît de Boigne.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Mahadji skillfully rebuilt Maratha prestige in the North following the 1761 debacle and reorganized his forces along European lines under de Boigne, creating elite brigades. [Primary Reference: Modern Indian History by Bipan Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the title 'Wakil-ul-Mutlaq':
1. It was conferred upon Mahadji Sindhia by Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II.
2. It made the Sindhia the supreme executive deputy of the Mughal Emperor, granting immense political authority.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. In 1785, Shah Alam II conferred the title of Wakil-ul-Mutlaq on Mahadji, making him the regent plenipotentiary of the Mughal Empire, which Mahadji cleverly had the Peshwa designated as the nominal principal while he acted as deputy. [Primary Reference: Spectrum's A Brief History of Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Anglo-Maratha Wars and the Sindhias:
1. Daulat Rao Sindhia was defeated during the Second Anglo-Maratha War and signed the Treaty of Surji-Anjangaon in 1803.
2. The treaty allowed the Sindhias to retain total control over Delhi, Agra, and Rajputana without any British interference.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Daulat Rao Sindhia suffered defeats by General Arthur Wellesley and Lord Lake, leading to the 1803 Treaty of Surji-Anjangaon. Statement 2 is incorrect: Under this treaty, Sindhia had to cede strategic territories including Delhi, Agra, and Ganga-Yamuna doab to the British. [Primary Reference: Modern Indian History by Bipan Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Gwalior state during the 1857 Revolt:
1. Maharaja Jayajirao Sindhia actively joined the rebel forces and led the siege of Cawnpore.
2. Despite his army mutinying and joining the revolt, Jayajirao Sindhia personally remained loyal to the British.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Jayajirao did not join the rebels; rather, he fled to Agra to seek British help when his troops mutinied. Statement 2 is correct: While the Gwalior contingent joined Tantia Tope and Rani Lakshmibai, the Maharaja remained steadfastly loyal to the British Crown. [Primary Reference: Spectrum's A Brief History of Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the architectural and cultural legacy of the Sindhias:
1. The Jai Vilas Palace in Gwalior was constructed by Jayajirao Sindhia and exhibits European architectural influences.
2. The Sindhia dynasty strictly prohibited temple construction and patronage of classical arts to conserve state finances.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Jai Vilas Palace (1874) was built by Jayajirao Sindhia, designed in European styles. Statement 2 is incorrect: The Sindhias were generous patrons of art, music, and temple architecture, famously restoring ghats in Varanasi and building notable temples. [Primary Reference: Archaeological Survey of India / Cultural Gazetteer of MP]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the geopolitical status of the Sindhias in late 18th-century India:
1. They successfully maintained complete neutrality between the British East India Company and the French interests in India.
2. Mahadji Sindhia's dominance in North India made him the principal arbiter in Delhi politics and the most powerful Maratha sardar of his era.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Far from neutrality, the Sindhias actively engaged with French military officers (like de Boigne) while clashing militarily and diplomatically with the British. Statement 2 is correct: Mahadji's control over Delhi and the Mughal emperor cemented his position as the preeminent Maratha leader. [Primary Reference: Modern Indian History by Bipan Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the integration of Gwalior into independent India:
1. Maharaja Jiwajirao Scindia acceded to the Indian Union in 1947 and later became the Rajpramukh of Madhya Bharat.
2. Gwalior was immediately declared an independent republic by its citizens without joining any union.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Jiwajirao Scindia signed the Instrument of Accession and later served as Rajpramukh of Madhya Bharat. Statement 2 is incorrect: Gwalior did not become an independent republic; it smoothly integrated into the Dominion of India through Patel's state integration framework. [Primary Reference: White Paper on Indian States]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the military administrative reforms of Mahadji Sindhia:
1. He relied entirely on traditional irregular Maratha cavalry and refused to recruit any European mercenaries.
2. He established cannon foundries and arsenals in Agra and other centers to make his army self-sufficient in modern weaponry.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Mahadji actively recruited European officers and raised disciplined regular infantry battalions, moving beyond traditional irregular cavalry. Statement 2 is correct: To sustain his modern army, he set up ordnance factories and foundries at Agra and elsewhere. [Primary Reference: Jadunath Sarkar / Military History of Marathas]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the socio-political position of the Sindhias in 18th-century India:
1. They originated from the Kunbi/Maratha community and successfully carved out a major sovereign princely state from the collapsing Mughal provinces in Malwa and Gwalior.
2. Their rise marked the complete elimination of Brahmin political influence within the Maratha Confederacy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The Sindhias belonged to the Kunbi caste and established a powerful state in Malwa and Gwalior amidst Mughal decline. Statement 2 is incorrect: Brahmin political influence (such as the Chitpavan Peshwas and various Brahmin diplomats/administrators like the Hingnes) remained prominent throughout the Maratha Confederacy. [Primary Reference: NCERT History / Maratha Social History]
